title: Dashboard tiering & telemetry cost cookbook
content:
Purpose:

This is a pragmatic working doc to capture a repeatable pattern for dashboard tiering tied to telemetry cost tradeoffs. The goal: give product/ops/eng a lightweight decision matrix to choose what signals to keep hot, what to sample, and what to tier off to cheaper retention, so we can preserve operator workflows while controlling query/ingestion cost.

Context / motivation:
- Obs budget is growing faster than our token-serving costs in some tenants; dashboards are the visible surface.
- We have many panels that are used rarely but cost a lot in query time/ingest.
- Operators complain about missing traces for certain fallback flows.
- Need a reproducible pattern to onboard new model rollouts without exploding trace/metric budgets.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Dashboard tier definitions (mission-critical -> audit -> archival)
- Sampling & retention heuristics per tier (metrics + traces + spans + session logs)
- Decision matrix for signal fitness (accuracy vs cost vs discovery value)
- Small probe design pattern for synthetic checks linked to panels
- Rollout checklist for changing retention/sampling on a route or model

Quick summary: proposed tiers
- Tier 0 (Operational SLOs / Live Ops): 30d retention for metrics at 1m granularity, traces sampled at 100% for error/latency >= p99 triggers, session stitching retained 7d. Panels: SLO, customer-impacting alerts, per-tenant latency heatmaps.
- Tier 1 (Investigation / Rollouts): 14d retention for metrics at 1m gran, traces sampled adaptively (see sampling rules), session context retained 3d, problem-case trace replays retained 30d if flagged. Panels: rollout dashboards, canary cohorts, kv-cache warmth.
- Tier 2 (Exploration / Cost-slim): 72h retention for metrics at 5m gran, traces sampled at 0.5% baseline with inference-driven upsampling for anomalies, session logs TTL 24h. Panels: long-tail trends, usage cohorts, quota burn down.
- Tier 3 (Archive / Audit): aggregated rollups only (daily / weekly), traces are not retained, raw logs are exported to cold storage on demand and gated by compliance requests.

Decision matrix (how to map a panel/signal to a tier) — quick checklist:
- Does this panel feed an SLO or an oncall alert? -> Tier 0
- Is this panel only used during rollouts and debugging (weekly/monthly)? -> Tier 1
- Is this used for occasional business questions (quarterly)? -> Tier 2
- Is it legally required or audit-only? -> Tier 3
- If unsure, fallback: make it Tier 1 with feature-flagged retention reduction after 30 days.

Metric definitions / shorthand (for reuse across dashboards):
- request_count: count of inference requests (tagged by model, route, tenant)
- token_out_count: sum of tokens emitted (approx billing token) — used for unit cost attribution
- p50_latency_ms, p90_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms — operate at service boundary (after routing/fallback)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: ratio of requests served from KV prefix cache vs cold path
- prefix_warmth_index: heuristically computed (unique prefixes warmed / request volume) — low-cost probe: compute daily aggregation only

Sampling recommendations (traces & spans):
- Baseline sampling: 0.1% across all traffic (Tier 2 by default)
- Adaptive upsampling: increase to 100% for requests that meet any of: error=true, latency > p99_route_threshold, model_variant != baseline, rollout=true
- Severity-weighted reservoir: keep more traces for high-severity customers (tags: enterprise=true) while keeping lower-sensitivity tenants at baseline sampling. This is controlled by tenant-weight in the sampler config (configurable per-dedicated-pool).
- Prefix-aware sampling for kv-cache debug: for requests with kv_cache_miss=true and prefix_length>16, sample at 5% to surface cold-cache root causes.
- Trace retention labeling: traces flagged during investigation get label investigation:true and extended retention (30d) — automatic TTL removal job.

Probes / synthetic checks (cheap design to keep dashboards meaningful):
- Probe types: simple synthetic token-generation probes, kv-cache-warmness probe, route-fallback probe.
- Cadences: live SLO probes at 1m; diagnostic probes (kv-warmness) at 10m; long-running scenario (fallback path) at 30m.
- Probe outputs should be a small set of metrics (probe_success, probe_latency_ms, probe_variant) and a single short trace id per probe run to link back if needed.
- Place probes under Tier 0 if they are used for alerting; otherwise Tier 1.

Cost model notes (very rough):
- Metric ingestion cost dominates high-cardinality metrics (per-tenant, per-model, per-route tags). Aim to move non-actionable high-cardinality panels to rollups.
- Tracing cost dominated by both ingestion rate and retention window; every 10x reduction in sampling yields roughly 6–8x reduction in cost due to indexing overhead.
- Dashboards with many widgets that ping slow queries (GROUP BY tenant) should be moved behind lightweight aggregated views or materialized daily rollups.

Dashboard design & UX heuristics (operator-focused):
- On-call home panel: <8 widgets, each with single-click drilldown to a filtered investigation page
- Investigation panel: grouped by hypothesis (latency, errors, kv-cache, routing) rather than by metric type
- Rollout panel: include cohort decomposition (by model variant, region, tier) and a synthetic probe timeline
- Cost-aware widgets: annotate each widget with an approximate monthly query cost (low / med / high) so owners can prioritize slimming.

Rollout checklist for changing sampling/retention on a route/model:
1) Create a small canary to lower retention on a non-critical tenant and measure impact on investigations (2 weeks)
2) Add feature flag to control sampler config for that route/model
3) Run both before/after probes for 72h and compare false-negatives in alert triggers
4) If acceptable, apply tier change with staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor operator feedback
5) Post-rollout audit: confirm any open investigation traces were not impacted; revert if operator pain > threshold

Operational playbook snippets (for oncall):
- If alert fires and trace missing: run targeted probe with trace-enabled flag; if probe reproduces, escalate to telemetry oncall to temporarily bump sampling for affected routes
- If dashboard latency spikes on a frequently queried panel: switch panel to cached rollup view and create incident note to review the query plan

Example sampler config (pseudocode human-readable):
- baseline_sampling_pct: 0.1
- upsample_rules:
  - error == true -> 100%
  - latency_ms > p99_threshold -> 100%
  - tenant_tier == enterprise -> min(1%, high_weight)
  - kv_cache_miss == true and prefix_length > 16 -> 5%
- retention_by_label:
  - investigation:true -> 30d
  - default -> tier_retention_map[route_tier]

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- How to quantify "discovery value" of a panel empirically? Can we instrument quick surveys or usage counters in Grafana to measure "time-to-first-investigation"?
- Are we comfortable with per-tenant severity-weighted sampling from a compliance angle? Need legal review for EU data residency and sampling logic.
- Mechanism for programmatic rehydration of archived traces for audits (cost & latency expectations).
- Should we auto-expire rare metric tags (e.g., ad-hoc experiment flags) after 30d to reduce cardinality?

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- A. Martinez: prototype tiering config in telemetry-configs repo; PR by 2024-12-01
- L. Chen: implement probe types and add synthetic probe dashboard; demo 2024-10-20
- P. Kapoor: run 2-week canary for one medium-traffic model route to test sampling heuristics; start 2024-11-05
- Noah Rivera: write oncall quickcard for trace-missing workflow; 2024-10-25

Notes-to-self / rough drafts:
- Keep the default baseline super low (0.1%) so budgeting is predictable; rely on adaptive upsampling for coverage
- We need a small set of tenant tags (enterprise/psr/low-sensitivity) fed into sampling config at routing time
- Consider a daily job that suggests panels for downgrade based on last-used-by-oncall metric and monthly query cost

References & links:
- Confluence: OBS Telemetry cost model (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1218)
- Jira: Keep an eye on JIRA-OBS-3401 for the rollout feature flag work
- GitHub: telemetry-configs PR #27 has the initial sampler parsing code (see linked_artifacts above)

If helpful, next step: convert this into a lightweight RFC with a small config prototype and one experimental rollout.
